questions.solution_html:

questions.question: How can proxies improve the editing experience for editors with slower computers or systems? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• How can proxies improve the editing experience for editors with slower computers or systems?
  • Proxies are low-resolution, low-bitrate versions of the original media, making them less
  • demanding on the computer's CPU and GPU, thus allowing for smoother, real-time playback
  • and editing.

questions.question: What is RAID 0, and what are its advantages and disadvantages in data storage? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is RAID 0, and what are its advantages and disadvantages in data storage?
  • RAID 0 (Striping): Data is split and written across multiple drives. Advantages: Fastest
  • performance, no capacity loss. Disadvantages: No redundancy (if one drive fails, all data is lost).

  • web/playback.

  • rigorous backup of original files.

questions.question: Provide a comprehensive explanation of how to choose the right bitrate for a video project, considering factors like resolution, frame rate, and delivery method. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Provide a comprehensive explanation of how to choose the right bitrate for a video project,
  • considering factors like resolution, frame rate, and delivery method.
  • Bitrate determines data flow (quality/file size). Higher resolution/frame rate generally needs a
  • higher bitrate to maintain quality.
  • The delivery method is key: Streaming (e.g., YouTube) has specific, moderate bitrate
  • recommendations; Broadcast/Archive needs very high bitrates for maximum quality. Balance
  • quality, file size, and target platform requirements.

questions.question: Compare and contrast the process of importing media versus ingesting media in a professional workflow. / [CO2] [6x5 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast the process of importing media versus ingesting media in a professional
  • workflow.
  • Importing is the simple act of linking a file to an editing project (e.g., linking an MP4).
  • Ingesting is a more structured, professional process that often involves copying the files (with
  • verification), backing up, transcoding (converting format), and adding metadata before the files
  • are available for editing.

questions.question: Discuss how to resolve issues related to incompatible proxy formats or settings in an editing project. Provide steps to check and fix common compatibility issues between proxy and full-resolution media. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss how to resolve issues related to incompatible proxy formats or settings in an editing
  • project. Provide steps to check and fix common compatibility issues between proxy and full-
  • resolution media.
  • Resolution: Ensure the proxy and original media have the same timecode, frame rate, and
  • aspect ratio. Incompatibility often arises from these mismatches or incorrect proxy creation
  • settings.
  • Fixing Steps: Check/Verify Original Media Properties (timecode, frame rate). Delete
  • Incompatible Proxies. Re-create Proxies using settings identical to the original media's
  • parameters (except resolution/bitrate). Use the editing software's "Relink/Re-match" function
  • to connect the original media to the new proxies.

questions.question: Explain in detail the importance of implementing redundancy in backup systems and how it helps to prevent data loss in visual editing workflows. Provide examples of redundancy techniques used in RAID systems and mirrored drives. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain in detail the importance of implementing redundancy in backup systems and how it
  • helps to prevent data loss in visual editing workflows. Provide examples of redundancy
  • techniques used in RAID systems and mirrored drives.
  • Importance: Redundancy is having multiple copies of data/system components to ensure
  • continuity even if one fails. It is critical in visual editing where data loss can mean losing weeks
  • of work. Helps prevent loss by allowing a system or workflow to recover instantly from a single
  • point of failure. Examples: RAID 5/6 (uses parity data for drive recovery); Mirrored Drives
  • (RAID 1) (identical copy of data on a second drive).

questions.question: Describe a scenario where poor file organization led to significant delays or complications during post-production. How could this have been prevented through better media management practices? / [CO2] [12x2 = 24]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe a scenario where poor file organization led to significant delays or complications
  • during post-production. How could this have been prevented through better media
  • management practices?
  • Scenario: An editor starts a film by dumping all footage, graphics, audio, and project files into a
  • single, unorganized folder. Months later, a missing sound effect or an old sequence cannot be
  • located, leading to a frantic, time-consuming search that delays the final delivery.
  • Prevention: Implement a standardized, consistent folder structure from the start (e.g., separate
  • folders for Footage, Audio, Graphics, Project Files, Exports). Use clear, standardized file
  • naming conventions (e.g., Date_Scene_Take) and use the editing software's Bins (folders) to
  • mirror this structure.
